name: STAR Orbit — Sun vector, beta angle and cylindrical eclipse
summary: Low-precision geocentric Sun vector for 1950-2050 (measured within 0.0097 deg of JPL DE440 apparent), orbit beta angle and cylindrical shadow test; every function returns finite values or raises ValueError.
reference: Vallado, Fundamentals of Astrodynamics and Applications, Example 5-1 (Sun position vector): 2006 April 2, 0h UTC -> 0.9771945, 0.1924424, 0.0834308 AU (mean equator and equinox of date)
reference_observed: each component within 1.2e-6 AU of the printed values; direction within 6.4e-5 deg

na.G-14: no performance requirement declared by any user

review.G-04: astronomical units, degrees; r_sat and body radius in the caller's unit; frame = mean equator and equinox of date, stated in docstring and README
review.G-06: no external data at run time; cross-check uses JPL DE440 (de440s.bsp) through SPICE, astropy and PyEphem
review.G-08: pure functions, standard library only, no IO
review.G-13: ValueError for every invalid input and for dates outside the stated validity; no iteration
